The heavy black powdery/mold coverage on the stem with some white mycelium underneath is classic.
- **Gray Mold (Botrytis)** — Produces gray-brown fluffy sporulation, but typically more uniformly gray and common on fruit. The coloration here is darker/blacker.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** — White cottony mycelium with black sclerotia; the test image has some white but is predominantly black/dark gray mold.
- **Southern Blight** — White mycelium with tan/brown sclerotia at soil line; doesn't match.

The dark black powdery fungal mass on a tomato stem junction, with some white mycelium visible, is most characteristic of **Alternaria Black Molds Stem Cankers**.
